He does not lay the house's omissions across his own kept empty intervals, for a joining would want a payer and none stands; the absence of the joining is itself kept, entered nowhere and not spent (T071/T072, T061/T082). On the 102nd answer the finding gets its physical counterpart: the little silence after a count that ended in the room that does not touch is kept **empty** on its own place, no rhythm carried across it and nothing supplied to make a stroke where there was none --- an empty object laid beside the held one and apart from it, a keeping and not a miss, not a longer reach, a hearing, a seventh, a stopping, a payment, a held change, a key, a power or a rule. Advanced, none paid: T071/T072 (261, 262 and 263 exact, six months and eighty-one through eighty-three days, told by nobody); T088 (fire's fifth unpaid the same three days, its payer unnamed); T061/T082 (answers 97--102, six hearings with no seventh, three counts in three places that do not agree, told bell beside heard, told figure beside paid, the file exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air, the empty interval of the 102nd kept and not crossed); T077 (grain lifted for damp and turned under wool, unfigured, the arithmetic on Smoke 30 that will not know its cost); T080 (Ilva glimpsed once on Smoke 23, strip unread, ninth hand nine, no tenth); T101 (five askings held, no sixth, no witness, no row named); T009/T013/T092 and T098 (seven walked-around places, two unswept lines, the hand that did not come back carried and not named); T058/T079 (widow's mark untouched; a yard, rack, well and bed are not openings; the next real opening the first firing of Frost); T100 (charcoal unread behind the finger on top of the shelf's front edge); T083/T085 (frost called weather, joined to nothing); T064 (wrong glaze wind off High Kiln a direction arrived nowhere, no fourth likeness made a cause); T036/T076 and T006 (ninth stopping remembered on all three days, seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, loan uncalled, warm stone cold); T035/T031/T062 and T065/T095 (meal-fine dust, men unnamed in the back room, damper's double bite, burned slate at four, shut-room tellings at two); T060/T086 (one crust, gap unnamed, no third). Nothing was joined, named, opened, called, paid or ended, no payer named and no lesson made of the one opening before Smoke 1.

Chapter 71 is written and closed: Days 264–266, Smoke 25–27, Fifthday to Seventhday, three lived days in six scenes, each day opened by its own `\daymark` and lived in two full scenes, nothing skipped, poured into another or summarised. There was no new named character with a real role who was not already on a sheet; no Account-day, market, Cross or bell in these three days, Smoke 30 (Day 269), the third and last reading of the second firing, standing three mornings ahead and not brought early, and the first firing of Frost (Day 271) far off. **The chapter's one meaningful change, advanced and not paid:** on Smoke 26 Sella drew the wool wholly back from the dressed grain and turned it piece by piece in the flat of her hand for damp and rot, setting each piece down where it lay, covering it and giving no figure, and the boy kept the finding that a thing can be examined as closely as a hand can examine it and still enter nothing on a place of its own — not a lesson, a grievance or a doctrine, and not laid across the house's not-doings or his own kept gaps, for a joining would want a payer and none stood; on Smoke 27 she turned it once with a lighter touch and learned nothing, and he kept the not-learning as a finding with no payer (T077, T061/T082). A second shaping, advanced and not paid: on Smoke 26 an ownerless voice reported over the boards that somebody had been asking which row went quiet — a report of an asking, not a sixth asking — and the boy set it beside the five askings with a finger between; still no witness stands, no row is named and no sixth asking has become a hearing (T101 advanced, unpaid). A third, physical: on the hundred and eighth answer the hand went past the river's next low note to the one after it, holding across two of the river's intervals with the silence between kept empty and no second house count borrowed, an honest coordination and not a reach, hearing, seventh, stopping, payment, held change, key, power or rule; he made nothing of the likeness to the handled grain and would not let it stand up as a gift (T061/T082). Advanced, none paid: T071/T072 (264, 265 and 266 exact, six months and eighty-four through eighty-six days, told by nobody); T088 (fire's fifth unpaid the same three days, payer unnamed); T061/T082 (answers 103–108, one hundred and eight honest answers on the sixth place, the file exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air, six hearings beside and never among with no seventh, three counts in three places that do not agree, told bell beside heard, told figure beside paid, two intervals and the empty silence kept on three places, no joining); T077 (grain corner-lifted on the 25th, turned piece by piece and covered on the 26th, turned once with a lighter touch on the 27th, unfigured throughout, the arithmetic on Smoke 30 that will not know its cost); T080 (Ilva glimpsed once on Smoke 26 at the well, ninth hand nine, strip unread, no tenth); T101 (five askings with one further shaping, advanced and unpaid, no sixth asking, no witness, no row named); T009/T013/T092 and T098 (seven walked-around places, two unswept lines, the hand that did not come back carried and not named); T058/T079 (widow's mark untouched; morning, hearth, bed, basket, rack, well, road and dusk not openings; the next real opening the first firing of Frost); T100 (charcoal unread behind the finger on top of the shelf's front edge); T083/T085 (frost called weather, joined to nothing); T064 (wrong glaze wind off High Kiln a direction arrived nowhere, no second edge paid, no fourth likeness); T035/T031/T062 and T065/T095 (meal-fine dust, unnamed men in the back room, the damper's double bite, burned slate at four, shut-room tellings at two); T036/T076 and T006 (ninth stopping remembered on all three days, seventh year at its very end, loan uncalled, warm stone cold); T060/T086 (one crust, unnamed gap, no third). Planted and held: Smoke 30 (Day 269) and Frost 1 (Day 270) with its first firing (Day 271); the uncalled loan, the ungiven promise, the unseen witness, the nine hands, the private keepings and the three held changes deepen without being spent. Chapter 72 is written and closed: Days 267–269, Smoke 28–30, Eighthday to Tenthday, three lived days in six scenes, each day opened by its own `\daymark` and lived in two full scenes, nothing skipped, poured into another or summarised. There was no named character with a real role who was not already on a sheet; Berr Clay and Hessa Rale were on stage at the Cross and the road on Smoke 30, Ilva was seen once at the yard well on Smoke 29, the soft-cuffed clerk stayed set at the out-of-line landing, the green-mouthed woman and the foundling stayed sightings with no eighth of either, and no sixth hearing, no tenth stopping before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, no sixth asking and no witness for the row, no tenth record-first hand, no figure off the firing-stick, no calling of the loan, no payer named, no private record opened or read, no lesson made of the one opening before Smoke 1, no fourth likeness made a cause and no ending. **The chapter's one meaningful change, advanced and not paid:** on Smoke 30 the third and last reading of Smoke came to the Cross and the district's arithmetic changed for the third time in Smoke and cannot be changed back. Berr came up short off the clay road with the red cord folded square, wiped his thumb twice before touching nothing, held a narrow slate unopened, read *one in twelve, as the notice says* twice over the basket, called the levy, denied it with *your house*, never *I*, and went off with the box locked and the third true subtraction inside, believing he had done a kindness; the printed figure stood unchallenged, the figure read was still not the figure paid, and the figure read over the dressed grain covered under wool at home did not know what it cost, the space between unsigned. The boy kept the finding that a figure read a third time over the same basket is no nearer the covered thing than a chart over a covered body, that three readings are three and not one account, and that the not-knowing is as complete after the third as after the first — a finding with no payer, not a lesson, grievance or doctrine, and not laid across the house's not-doings, the covered grain or his own kept gaps (T071/T072, T077, T015/T041/T047, T061/T082). **A second physical advancement, also unpaid:** the hand answered six times, the hundred and ninth through the hundred and fourteenth, each an honest coordination on the sixth place and worth nothing at two inches of air; on the last the hand carried two of the house's rhythms across the empty interval and left the bell's gap in the square with a finger between, no stroke supplied to agree any three (T061/T082, T078). Chapter 73 is written and closed: Days 270–272, Frost 1–3, Firstday to Thirdday, three lived days in six scenes, each day opened by its own `\daymark` and lived in two full scenes, nothing skipped, poured into another or summarised. It opened **no new thread**, paid none and closed none; one hundred and one threads stand at the close (66 planted, 34 open, 1 paid), unchanged from the close of Chapter 72. There was no named character with a real role who was not already on a sheet; Ilva was seen once at the yard well on Frost 1, Berr Clay's unread arithmetic and the box up the road were named offstage, Garl was kept in objects with his name unspoken two hundred and seventy-two days, and no Account-day, market, Cross or bell came in these three days — the first firing of Frost on Frost 2 (Day 271) was earned by that morning's own light, and Frost 10 (Day 279), the month's first Account-day and market, stands six mornings beyond the close and was not brought early. **The chapter's one meaningful change, advanced and not paid:** on Frost 2, before any word and before the basket, Sella went to the kiln mouth, put her hand to the widow's mark for one breath, let go, lifted the clay lid with the back of a hand and tipped the carried coal under the back of a broken pot; the fire took, still answering four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should have stood, its payer unnamed two hundred and seventy-one days. Nobody praised it, nobody named what it mended, no slate was entered, no bond changed hands, no payer named and no lesson or sign made (T058/T079 and T088 advanced, **not paid**). It is the **fourth** opening under the household's roof, after Tallow 1, Ember 1 and Smoke 1; four are four and not a rule, and the next opening stands in a later month's first firing, far off and not hoped for. The mark was touched once before that kiln and at no shelf, well, rack, road, basket, yard, morning, hearth, afternoon, dusk or going of the light on Frost 1, 2 or 3, because a basket, a shelf and a dusk are not openings (T058/T079 held exactly). Advanced, none paid: T071/T072 (270, 271 and 272 kept exact, six months and ninety days through six months and ninety-two days, told by nobody, the answers one hundred and fifteen through one hundred and twenty filed on the sixth place and worth nothing at two inches of air); T061/T082 (the hundred and fifteenth a small intake and a down on the next low note with no house count borrowed; the sixteenth one house rhythm carried across the little silence after a count in the other room as an object, the silence not filled; the seventeenth held for the hold of a counted breath and down before the letting-go; the eighteenth held through one whole interval of the river; the nineteenth taking the intake and hold of a borrowed count and coming down before its letting-go; the twentieth held past that letting-go and through the silence, setting the held interval and the empty interval side by side with a finger between and neither made to agree with the fire's missing fifth — six honest coordinations, not reaches, hearings, sevenths, stoppings, payments, held changes, keys, powers or rules, and not allowed to stand up as gifts); T077 and T015/T041/T047 (the dressed grain turned beneath the wool for damp with a progressively lighter touch and given no figure, Smoke's third arithmetic unread up the clay road in Berr's locked box and the figure read still not the figure paid, the space between unsigned); T036/T076 and T006 (Tarn keeping six where the house can check and the seventh at the lip of the knife, bringing the ear-sentence to the calling word and stopping as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, the Seed 16 breath unspent, the loan uncalled and no collector up or down the clay road, the loft stone cold and unreconciled); T035/T031/T062/T065/T095 (Jorra parting dusty forearms from clean, speaking to the wheel and a pot before any person, withholding the full note known three turns ahead, putting the bent finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella's unfinished sentence, burned slate at four, shut-room tellings at two, three pot sayings with the premature Smoke 14 note apart, five askings with one shaping and no witness, *he's not Vail* sealed and the promise of the boy's name neither given nor withdrawn); T009/T013/T092 and T098 (the seven walked-around places gone around with a look and a wide step and no number, including the returning-line place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, carried and not named); T100 (charcoal unread behind the finger on top of the shelf's front edge); T080 held at **nine** with Ilva seen once on Frost 1 and her strip unread; T101 held at **five askings** with one shaping and no witness; T093/T094, T064, T078, T060/T086 carried. Nothing was opened, named, called, paid or ended; the count crossed into Frost 4 at 272 exact with 120 answerings and the fire's fifth unpaid the same number of days, its payer unnamed.

The boy filed the returned held beat on the shelf's own place beside the Day 161 fraction, the Day 166 beat and the Tallow 22 flagstone half-check, not a new place, not a fourth likeness standing up as a cause, not a reading, not a payment and not a doctrine (T100 advanced, **not paid**); on Frost 6 her finger stayed on top of the edge and the two breaths were not repeated and did not become a rule. Advanced, none paid: T071/T072 (273, 274 and 275 kept exact, complete, unspent and spoken by nobody, six months and ninety-three through ninety-five days); T088 (the carried fire's fifth unpaid the same three days, four low pulls under the floor with its payer unnamed); Held, not advanced: six hearings beside and never among with no seventh; five askings with one shaping and no witness; nine stoppings with no tenth; nine record-first hands with a finger between every pair; three pot sayings with the premature Smoke 14 note apart; burned slate at four and shut-room tellings at two; the seventh green a colour and the seventh shape a shape with no eighth; no third gap and no fourth likeness made a cause. Berr Clay comes up short off the clay road with the red wool cord folded square under his coat and the green of tasted lead glaze at one mouth-corner, wipes his thumb twice before touching nothing, holds a narrow slate unopened to his forearm, passes a finger over the figure, reads *one in twelve, as the notice says* low into the two hundred, calls the levy, denies it with *The levy is called. It is not called by me* and *your house*, never *I*, taking himself out of his own sentence as a hand goes out of a field before the dressing goes on, and goes off toward High Kiln with the box locked and the first true subtraction of Frost inside, believing he has done a kindness (T015/T041/T047 advanced, unpaid). The printed figure stands unchallenged and the figure read is still not the figure paid; the reading answers nothing for the man carried out on Day 188, the hand that went in on Seed 15 and did not come back, or the dressed grain lying covered under wool at the rack end and read over by a number that does not know what it cost, the space between figure and price unsigned (T077, T098 carried). Berr never looks into the basket and has entered that nowhere nowhere. Chapter 78 is written and closed: Days 285–287, Frost 16–18, Sixthday to Eighthday, three lived days in six scenes, each day opened by its own `\daymark` and lived in two full scenes, nothing skipped, poured into another or summarised. It opened **no new thread**, paid none and closed none; one hundred and one threads stand at the close (66 planted, 34 open, 1 paid), unchanged from the close of Chapter 77. There was no new named character with a real role who was not already on a sheet; Ilva was glimpsed once at the yard well on Frost 17 and given no figure, and no Account-day, market, Cross or bell came in these three days, Frost 20 (Day 289), the second Account-day, standing two mornings beyond the close and unbrought. **The chapter's one meaningful change, advanced and not paid (T061/T082, T071/T072, T088):** the hand answered six times, the hundred and forty-fifth through the hundred and fiftieth — a house rhythm carried across the river's interval; two intakes held apart with a finger between; an intake held past its letting-go and through the little silence; a bridge laid down as an object over the river's note; a letting-go kept whole on the same note; and the held interval and the empty interval set side by side with a finger between — and one hundred and fifty honest answers stood on the sixth place, exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air. The round threshold was held as an object and emphatically **not a doctrine**, for a doctrine is an account that has found a payer and none stands, and a gift wants a taker and nobody under this roof has taken anything; four openings in four months are four and not a rule. The count went 284 → 287 exact, six months and one hundred and five through one hundred and seven days told by nobody, with the fire's fifth unpaid the same three days and its payer unnamed. Chapter 79 is written and closed: Days 288–290, Frost 19–21, Ninthday to Firstday, Y.H. 813, three lived days in six scenes, each day opened by its own `\daymark` and lived in two full scenes, nothing skipped, poured into another or summarised. It opened **no new thread**, paid none and closed none; one hundred and one threads stand at the close (66 planted, 34 open, 1 paid), unchanged from the close of Chapter 78. There was no new named character with a real role who was not already on a sheet; Berr Clay, Hessa Rale, the soft-cuffed clerk at the landing and the two hundred at the Cross were on stage on Frost 20, the green-mouthed woman at the pot board and the foundling at the market's edge stayed sightings with no eighth of either, Ilva was offstage on all three days with her ninth strip unread, and no Account-day, market, Cross or bell came on Frost 19 or 21. **The chapter's one meaningful change, advanced and not paid (T015/T041/T047):** Frost's second Account-day comes to the Cross on Day 289; Berr Clay comes up short off the clay road with the red wool cord of his office folded square under his coat and the green of tasted lead glaze at one mouth-corner, wipes his thumb twice before touching nothing, holds a narrow slate unopened to his forearm, passes a finger over the figure and reads *one in twelve, as the notice says* low into the two hundred, the figure going over the basket once for the moot and once for the households that came late; he calls the levy, denies it with *The levy is called. It is not called by me* and *your house*, never *I*, taking himself out of his own sentence as a surgeon takes a hand out of a field before the dressing goes on, and goes off toward High Kiln with the box locked and the second true subtraction of Frost inside, believing he has done a kindness. The district's arithmetic changes a second time for the month and cannot be changed back; the printed figure stands unchallenged, the figure read is still not the figure paid, the twice-read figure is two and not one account, and the figure read over the dressed grain covered under wool at the rack end does not know what that grain cost, the space between unsigned. The reading answers nothing for the man carried out on Day 188, the hand that went in on Seed 15 or the covered grain. **The second movement, advanced and not paid (T080):** on the afternoon of Frost 19 an ownerless voice over the boards and the well-roof, with no owner standing anywhere to be asked, no room, no hand at a slate, no name, no figure, no confession and no cause, gives the Frost 14 saying a **second shaping** — what a runner carries in a slate that has a name in it — and goes on with the day as the yard says the weather. The boy takes it apart as a surgeon takes a wound apart and files it on a place of its own beside the first saying and beside Hessa Rale's eighth record-first hand with a finger between every pair: two shapings toward the far-off day she must choose whether to read what she has carried, not a hearing, not a seventh, not a tenth hand, not a cause, not a confession, not a joining, not a witness and **not paid**. It does not make Hessa a reader and is not joined to Ilva's strip a pace away, Berr's twice-wiped thumb, the soft-cuffed clerk's inward slate or the charcoal under the shelf; two shapings must not stand up as a rule, for a rule is an account that has found a payer and none stands. **The body and the hand:** the hand answers six times, the hundred and fifty-first through the hundred and fifty-sixth — the small intake of the fire's silence carried across the interval to the first morning's going; two intakes held apart with a finger between where the second shaping stands beside the first; the space between the moot's reading and the late households' reading set beside his own unnamed gap; the heard bell's gap beside a counted breath from the room whose floor does not touch his; an intake held past its letting-go and through the little silence left whole and empty; and the held interval and the empty interval set side by side with a finger between — and one hundred and fifty-six honest answers stand on the sixth place, exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air. The round threshold was held as an object and emphatically **not a doctrine**, for a doctrine is an account that has found a payer and none stands. The count went 287 → 290 exact, six months and one hundred and eight through one hundred and ten days told by nobody, with the fire's fifth unpaid the same three days and its payer unnamed; the surgeon's clean satisfaction was checked by the infant's louder want of the crust two inches off, and the checking is the work and not a virtue. | T101 | The question about the row — a voice with no owner asks over the boards which row a pot went quiet on, and the weather and the price of barley answer instead | Ch 59 (Grain 21, Day 230, Scene 6): over the boards of the Clay Yard, in the afternoon, a voice with no room, no hand at the kiln and no cause asks low which row the pot went quiet on; the weather answers first and the price of barley after it, and the voice goes off up the terrace while the row stands where it stood. The boy takes the question apart as a surgeon takes apart a wound — what it asks, where it stands, what it would want before any man could answer it, and who would have to stand under the answer to pay for it — and files it on a **seventh place of its own** with a finger between it and the three shapings of the pot saying, the fourth telling of the burned slate, the two shut-room tellings, the six hearings of the full note and the count. It is **not** a fourth shaping of the pot saying (a proverb and a question are different instruments), not a hearing, not a seventh of the full note, not a cause, not a name and not a fifth telling of the slate. A row is a place; a place wants a witness; a witness wants a day when somebody stands somewhere and can be asked. No witness stands yet. **Ch 60 (Grain 23, Day 232): advanced and not paid** — the question came back over the boards a **second** time in the same voice with no owner, no room, no hand at the kiln and no cause; the weather answered first and the price of barley after it, the voice went off up the terrace and the row stood where it stood. The boy set the second telling on the seventh place beside the first with a finger between the two and fingers between them and the three pot sayings, the fourth burned-slate telling, the two shut-room tellings, the six hearings and the count. Two askings are not one witness; a witness stands somewhere and can be asked, and none does. Still **not** a fourth shaping, a hearing, a seventh of the full note, a fifth telling of the slate, a cause, a name or a fifth witness — a seed for the far-off day a witness stands somewhere and can be asked. | Far off, when a witness stands somewhere and can be asked (no owner, room, hand at the kiln, figure or cause is given now); held on its own place beside the other directions arrived nowhere | planted |

*90 threads. Forty-eight stand planted at the close of Chapter 9 --- Chapter 9 opened no new thread, closed none and paid none; it advanced T001, T004, T007-T009, T013, T015, T023, T025, T031, T035, T036, T041, T044, T047, T058-T061, T065, T071-T073 and T076-T088, chiefly T082 (the nearly-full pot as the interval's first earthly answer, advanced and not paid), T083/T085 (honeyed ice, the opened hairline, the Singing Sill early, the high clay-heavy brook) and T086 (two crusts, no third). The pause in the neat dark hand has now been seen five times --- the flare, the birth-slate, the Cross on Stone 10, the Court's table on Stone 20 and the market's edge on Stone 30 --- and the fifth did not join the first four; the Drawing collector's hand still has no pause and stays in its own place. The flat note has five hearings from four sources and no sixth; Stone 13, Stone 17 and Stone 25 added three intervals, kept on a separate tray from the hearings, and Ilmen 6 added a nearly-full answer to the Stone 13 interval, filed on its own tray and not counted as a sixth. Day 38 will add the sixth hearing and the second from a person and will pay the hand-on-the-basket detail held from Ilmen 8; neither has been written. Two crusts lie side by side in the fold, one spent and one given, neither entered nor eaten. Five rooms --- birth room, kiln-house, death-house, Court's room and the neighbour's room two doors down --- hold the same bench, pot, draught and gap, and the boy has kept them apart on purpose. Low Kiln still reads one in twelve and gives out three, then two, then whatever the moot has already decided; the word forty has not been spoken. A passage changes the count and nothing else: the fifth sighting buys no word, no hand and no standing, and a week of keeping the count exactly buys a thumb on wicker the boy cannot spend.*

*Chapter 10 closes on Day 44, Ilmen 15, Y.H. 813, with the boy forty-four days old and nothing joined, paid or explained except a sound, a shape and a word. It opened no fifth pause and no seventh hearing; it paid T087's Day 38 payoff (the sixth hearing, the second from a person, out of a woman in the brook) and the hand-on-wicker detail held since Ilmen 8, advanced T004/T008/T044/T061/T073 and the first edge of T009's heresy as an omission, planted T089 (the pewter tin above the bed) and T090 (the clerk at the Fishstairs for an uncalled measure), and moved T024 from open to planted when Orra tied the forty-first knot and said the word into the basket. The count stands at six hearings from four sources plus one from a person, five unjoined pauses, three intervals, the told bell beside the heard bell, the nearly-full answer on its own tray, and four, four and a gap. Two crusts still lie in the fold and one will go missing on Day 45, with nobody saying who took it. Dessa is dead and stays dead; no collector was called and nobody named the omission. Fifty stand planted at the close of Chapter 10 (verified against the table: 50 planted, 39 open, 1 paid); T087 was paid, no thread was ended outright.

*Chapter 11 closes on Day 47, Ilmen 18, Y.H. 813, with the boy forty-seven days old and nothing joined, paid or explained except a shape that can now be read and a taking nobody will name. It opened T091 (the three hands on a tray) and moved T083 from open to planted; T086 paid its first edge on Day 46 --- the crust is gone, eaten by nobody, lifted in no one's sight and spoken of by nobody --- while its deeper payoff stays for ~1500. T001, T007–T009, T013, T023–T025, T035, T036, T041, T044, T047, T058–T061, T065, T071–T073, T076–T080, T082, T084–T086, T088–T090 were advanced; chiefly T024 (the knot's shape legible without its name, the word unspoken, the watching continued), T088 (the coal gone up with a bird, entered nowhere), T086 (the crust gone), T085/T083 (frost-bloom, ice going soft, higher brook, early low note, weak board heard-of), T090 (the clerk still set) and T071/T072 (the exact count carried). The six hearings stayed six from four sources plus one from a person, no seventh; the five pauses, the nearly-full note, the told bell, the absence shaped like a collection, the word and the knot, and the two women's cords all stayed on separate trays and unjoined. Ninety-one threads stand at the close of Chapter 11 (52 planted, 38 open, 1 paid); nothing was ended outright.**

*Chapter 12 is written and closed: Days 48–54, Ilmen 19–25, Y.H. 813, a seven-day passage chapter lived one dated entry at a time. It opened no new thread, paid none and closed none; it advanced T007–T009, T013, T015, T023–T025, T035, T036, T041, T047, T058–T061, T065, T071–T073, T076–T086, T089–T091 — chiefly T085 (frost-bloom written back, the oiled paper slack in its frame, a silence where an argument stood, more hairlines stopping short of the edge, the Singing Sill early, the high clay-heavy brook, all called weather), T083 (the weak plank walk board said plainly still there and trodden by nobody), T082 (a SECOND nearly-full answer to the Stone 13 interval, advanced and not paid), T077 (one in twelve printed and unchallenged over the basket, the thaw number from fist to mouth to shoulder and given to nobody), T023 (a fifth hidden note and the tin touched once unopened) and T086/T091 (one crust and an empty place carried seven days, the three hands still on their tray). The six hearings stayed six, five from four sources and one from a person, beside and never among; no seventh came, no sixth sighting of the neat dark hand, no joining of word, shape, cords, pauses or trays, and no accident made of the board. Ninety-one threads stand at the close of Chapter 12, unchanged from Chapter 11 (52 planted, 38 open, 1 paid); nothing was ended outright.

*Chapter 13 is written and closed: Days 55–60, Ilmen 26–30 and Silt 1, Y.H. 813, a six-day passage lived one dated entry at a time. It opened T092 (the new hairline of grey in the Vail corner, called thaw and not swept, toward the flood of Ch 14–15 and the later day a house is left where it is and still kept) and left T065 standing planted while planting its long-promised seed in the text: the Greybank saying of a counting room shut in the last war with the damper closed and men dead of the breath, told at the well as history eighteen leagues east, filed on its own tray beside the told bell, the heard bell and the kiln's gap with no cause written across it (T065, T078, T071/T072). No thread was paid and none was ended. T081 (House Silt entered as a room left where it is); T071/T072 and T077 (exact three days to Silt kept by the boy against the house's loaves, glances and an uncalled space at the shelf's end; the number for the thaw from fist to mouth to shoulder and given to nobody); Chapter 81 is written and closed: Days 294–296, Frost 25–27, Fifthday to Seventhday, Y.H. 813, three lived days in six full scenes, each day opened by its own `\daymark` and lived in two scenes well over eight hundred words, nothing skipped, poured into another or summarised. There was no market, Cross or bell on any of the three days; no new named character with a real role came on stage, no thread was opened, paid or closed, and one hundred and one threads stand as they stood at the close of Chapter 80 (66 planted, 34 open, 1 paid). **The chapter's one meaningful change, advanced and not paid (T080):** on the afternoon of Frost 26 Ilva of the firing work is seen a second time at the yard well, drawing with the pail against her knee, clay dried pale in her nail crescents and rack dust in one thumb seam; a neighbour with a pot asks what the month's firings have taken, an open slate lies on the stone lip with the writing turned toward its owner and nobody reading it aloud, and her hand goes toward her sleeve and stays there. The notched birch strip is not taken out, read, asked about, copied, counted or joined to the slate, and no figure comes off the wood; her eyes go to the asker and her mouth opens after both with a half-beat, answering the question put and not the one behind it: *Ask the pot what it cost. I keep the count, not the account.* The boy takes the order of reaching apart — hand to the record, eyes to the asker, mouth after both — and files it as the **ninth** record-first hand on its own place beside the eighth with a finger between every pair; he files **no tenth**, takes no figure off the wood, and sets the open slate's nearness on a place of its own as an absence rather than a joining. Ilva is offstage on Frost 25 and 27 and the strip stays in her sleeve; this makes her no reader, no party to an account and no witness, joins her to none of the other private keepings, and brings nothing under the Vail roof as lesson, figure, mending, cause or payment. The strip and the three shapings of the Frost 14 well-saying are held for the far-off hand that will lay the district's private keepings together. The hand files six answers, the **one hundred and sixty-third** through the **one hundred and sixty-eighth**, the last letting a small intake go whole on the river's note; the count goes 293 to 294 to 295 to 296 exact, six months and one hundred and fourteen through one hundred and sixteen days told by nobody, and the fire's fifth stays unpaid the same number of days with its payer unnamed. Frost goes out without a boundary drawn and Frost 30 (Day 299), the third and last Account-day, stands three mornings ahead and was not brought in or made a sign. Forward, not closed.

It opened **no new thread**, paid none and closed none; one hundred and one threads stand as they stood at the close of Chapter 81 (66 planted, 34 open, 1 paid). Frost went out without a boundary drawn and neither of the district's two habits of naming its months was corrected; there was no market, Cross or bell on Frost 28 and 29 and Frost 30 was the month's third and last Account-day and market, earned by its own morning. No new named character with a real role came on stage; Berr Clay and Hessa Rale were on stage at the Cross on Frost 30, Ilva was seen once at the well on Frost 28, the soft-cuffed clerk stayed set at the landing, and the green-mouthed woman and the foundling stayed sightings with no eighth of either. **The chapter's one meaningful change, advanced and not paid (T015/T041/T047):** on Frost 30 Frost's third reading came to the Cross and the district's arithmetic changed a third time for the month in a way that cannot be changed back. Berr Clay came up short off the clay road with the red wool cord folded square under his coat and the green of tasted lead glaze at one mouth-corner, under the hot clay the smell of nothing at all, wiped his thumb twice before touching nothing, held a narrow slate unopened to his forearm with the writing inward, passed a finger over the figure and read *One in twelve, as the notice says* low into the two hundred, sent the figure over the basket twice — once for the moot and once for the late households — called the levy and denied it with *The levy is called. It is not called by me* and *your house*, never *I*, taking himself out of his own sentence as a surgeon takes a hand out of a field before the dressing goes on, and went off toward High Kiln with the box locked and Frost's third true subtraction inside beside the first two, believing he had done a kindness. The printed figure stands unchallenged, the figure read is still not the figure paid, and no signature stands on the space between; the twice-spoken figure is two sayings and not one account. The reading answered nothing for the dressed grain covered under wool at the rack end, read over a third time by a number that did not know its cost, nor for the man carried out on Day 188 nor the hand that went in on Seed 15. The boy kept Frost's first, second and third arithmetics on three places with a finger between, three and not one account, and kept the finding on a place of its own with no payer — not a lesson, grievance, mending or doctrine, and not laid across the house's not-doings, the covered grain or his own kept gaps; the edges nearly touched and the finger went between. Advanced, not paid; nothing settled by it.

Chapter 83 is written and closed: Days 300–302, Bone 1–3, Firstday to Thirdday, Y.H. 813, three lived days in six full scenes, each day opened by its own dated `\daymark` and lived in two scenes well over eight hundred words, nothing skipped, poured into another or summarised. It opened **no new thread**, paid none and closed none; one hundred and one threads stand as they stood at the close of Chapter 82 (66 planted, 34 open, 1 paid). Bone came on without a boundary drawn and neither of the district's two habits of naming the months was corrected; there was no market, Cross or bell on any of the three days, and Bone 10 (Day 309), the month's first Account-day, stood seven mornings ahead and was not brought early. No new named character with a real role came on stage; the Cold Acre hunter who carried a hare across his shoulders and the woman who asked what the carrying cost were walk-ons with no sheet, Ilva was seen once at the yard well on Bone 2, and Sella, Tarn, Jorra and Garl-in-objects went on in their old grammar. **The chapter's one meaningful change, advanced and not paid (T058/T079, T088):** the household fired in Bone on Bone 2, earned by that morning's own light. Sella went to the kiln mouth before the basket, put her hand to the widow's mark on its cord for one breath, let go, lifted the clay lid with the back of a hand and tipped the carried coal under the back of a broken pot; the fire took and answered four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should have stood, its payer unnamed three hundred and one days then three hundred and two. Nobody praised the opening, named what it mended, entered a slate, raised a hand to a face, said a number over the basket or made a lesson of it. **Five openings in five months** (Days 150, 180, 240, 271 and 301) are five and not a rule; the four behind are not looked at again as signs, payments or menders, and the fifth did not make a sixth due. The widow's mark was not touched again at shelf, well, rack, basket, yard, morning, hearth, afternoon, going of the light or small hours on any of the three days: the hand goes to it before the kiln and at no other hour. The boy kept the fifth opening on a place of its own with a finger between it and his own kept gaps, did not lay it across the house's not-doings or the covered grain, and named no payer to what it mended. He read it as a controlled reconnection under a clamp, heat returning from outside paid for by a man nobody in the room would name; the surgeon's knowing bought nothing at two inches of air. A second texture, not a thread: on Bone 1 a hunter come down from Cold Acre waited at the well with a hare across his shoulders, the carrying judged by the arm that did it, and answered a woman's question about the cost with the weather before going off toward the north gate road, so the month's hunting and repairs came into the yard as directions and not figures (T077 advanced, not paid).

Chapter 85 is written and closed: Days 306–308, Bone 7–9, Seventhday to Ninthday, Y.H. 813, three lived days in six full scenes, each day opened by its own dated `\daymark` and lived in two scenes well over eight hundred words, nothing skipped, poured into another or summarised. It opened **no new thread**, paid none and closed none; one hundred and one threads stand as they stood at the close of Chapter 84 (66 planted, 34 open, 1 paid). Bone went on without a boundary drawn and neither of the district's two habits of naming its months was corrected; there was no market, Cross or bell on any of the three days, and Bone 10 (Day 309), the month's first Account-day and market, stood one morning beyond the close and was not brought early. No new named character with a real role came on stage: Sella, Tarn, Jorra, Garl-in-objects and Ilva-once-at-the-well-on-Bone-7 went on in their old grammar; the hare-carrier toward the north gate road, the woman with a pot asking the month's cost, the early-and-late thaw arguers answered with *Yes, house* and the men unnamed going low into the back room before first grey were walk-ons with no sheet. **The chapter's one meaningful change, advanced and not paid (T062/T035/T031, T036/T076, T061/T082):** at the going of the light on Bone 8, while Jorra's bent finger stood in the cold damper ahead of Sella's unfinished sentence and she allowed the end of it to arrive at the pot, Tarn's broom checked half a beat behind the standing finger on the flagstones and went on toward the road without a word or a turn of the head — the Seed 22 half-check and the Day 171 flagstone movement returned changed after a hundred and thirty-six days. The flagstones kept the place where the stroke stopped as a shallow brightness at the edge of the patch nobody swept; neither man named the other's silence; the loan that can hear was still uncalled and no collector came up or went down the clay road. The boy filed the returned half-check on the flagstone's own place beside the Day 161 damper fraction, the Day 166 shelf beat and the Frost 5 returned beat: **four held changes on four places**, and he forbade them to stand up and call themselves a rule, for a rule is an account that has found a payer and none stood. It was not repeated on Bone 7 or Bone 9, is not a hearing, a seventh, a tenth stopping, a payment, a reconciliation, a mercy, a gift, a doctrine or a rule, and Bone 10 carries it unchanged, held for the far-off hand that will lay the district's private keepings together. The hand answered six times, the **one hundred and eighty-seventh** through the **one hundred and ninety-second**, each exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air, an object and not a power, no payer named to any; the count went 305 to **308 exact**, six months and one hundred and twenty-six through one hundred and twenty-eight days told by nobody, with the fire's fifth unpaid and Garl's name unspoken the same three numbers of days. The file lay open on the towel at the close with every gap left gap, and nothing was joined, named, opened, called, paid or ended.

Chapter 87 is written and closed: Days 312–314, Bone 13–15, Thirdday to Fifthday, Y.H. 813, three lived days in six full scenes, each day opened by its own dated `\daymark` and lived in two scenes well over eight hundred words, nothing skipped, poured into another or summarised. **No new thread was opened, none was paid and none was closed; one hundred and one threads stand as they stood at the close of Chapter 86 (66 planted, 34 open, 1 paid).** There was no market, Cross or bell on any of the three days and nothing from Bone 10, 11 or 12 came into them as sign, lesson, mending, cause or payment. No new named character with a real role came on stage: Corin/Dan, Sella Vail, Tarn, Jorra Vail and Garl-in-objects went on in their old grammar, Ilva was seen once at the well on Bone 14, and the Cold Acre hare-carrier, the woman with a pot, the barrow man and the unnamed yard workers were walk-ons with no sheet. **The chapter's one meaningful change, advanced and not paid (T060/T086, T061/T082):** at the end of the morning of Bone 15 the hand outside the wool came up an inch toward the river's note, took its small intake and let it go whole, and then, for the first time, did not come straight down to the fold; it stayed at the inch for the space of the note's fading, held and not reaching, while the two inches to the crust remained unclosed. The surgeon read a clamp left a moment after the bleeding had stopped or a tourniquet not yet released; the infant read a hand that had not given up wanting the crust; both were true and neither won. He filed it as answer 203, a new object on a place of its own on the sixth place: not a reach, a gift, a power, a seventh hearing, a tenth stopping, a fifth held change, a fifth likeness or a payment, with no payer named, not laid across the four held changes on four places, the covered grain, the four arithmetics or his own kept gaps — the edges nearly touch and the finger goes between. It was **not made again** at the going of the light: answer 204 came straight down. One staying is a keeping; two would be a habit, and a habit would want a payer. Held for the far-off hand that will read the file.

Chapter 89 is written and closed: Days 318–320, Bone 19–21, Ninthday to Firstday, Y.H. 813, three lived days in six full scenes, each day opened by its own dated `\daymark` and lived in two scenes well over eight hundred words, nothing skipped, poured into another or summarised. **No new thread was opened, none was paid and none was closed; one hundred and one threads still stand (66 planted, 34 open, 1 paid), unchanged from the close of Chapter 88.** There was no named character with a real role who was not already on a sheet: Corin/Dan, Sella Vail, Tarn, Jorra Vail and Garl-in-objects went on in their old grammar, Ilva was seen once at the yard well on Bone 20, Berr Clay and Hessa Rale were on stage at the Cross and on the road on the twentieth, the soft-cuffed clerk stayed set at the out-of-line landing, and the green-mouthed woman at the pot board and the foundling at the market's edge stayed sightings with no eighth of either; there was no market, Cross or bell on Bone 19 or 21, and Bone 30 (Day 329), the month's third and last reading, stood nine mornings ahead and was not brought early. **The chapter's one meaningful change, advanced and not paid (T015/T041/T047):** Bone's second reading came to the Cross on Day 319. Berr Clay came up short off the clay road with the red wool cord folded square under his coat and the green of tasted lead glaze at one mouth-corner, wiped his thumb twice on his apron before touching nothing, held a narrow slate unopened to his forearm with the writing inward, passed a finger over the figure, read *One in twelve, as the notice says* low into the two hundred and sent the figure twice over the basket — once for the moot and once for the late households — called the levy and denied it with *The levy is called. It is not called by me* and *your house*, never *I*, taking himself out of his own sentence as a surgeon takes a hand out of a field before the dressing goes on, and went off up the clay road with the box locked and Bone's second true subtraction inside beside the three of Frost and the first of Bone, believing he had done a kindness. **Five arithmetics of the year now stand behind one printed figure:** five are five and not one account, one in twelve stands unchallenged, the figure read is still not the figure paid and no signature stands on the space between; a rule made from five would want a payer put under all five and none stood, and the boy kept the finding on a place of its own with no payer, not a lesson, grievance, mending, doctrine or rule. He did not lay it across the house's not-doings, the dressed grain covered under wool, the four held changes on four places, the stayed-at-the-inch object, the early letting-go of Bone 17 or his own kept gaps — the edges came near to touching and the finger went between. The reading answered nothing for the hare gone into the weather, the hand that went in on Seed 15, the man carried out on Day 188 or the grain read over by a number that did not know its cost, and nothing under the Vail roof was settled by it. The hand answered six times, the **two hundred and eleventh** through the **two hundred and sixteenth**, each a small intake let go whole on the river's note, coming straight down because the note had done before the hand came down, so no letting-go was early again and the hand did not stay; **two hundred and sixteen honest answers** stand on the sixth place, each an object and not a power. Neither the staying of Bone 15 nor the early letting-go of Bone 17 was made again; they remain two objects on two places with a finger between them, neither a habit, a way, a fifth held change or a payer. The count went 317 → 318 → 319 → 320 exact, six months and one hundred and thirty-eight through one hundred and forty days told by nobody, with the fire's fifth unpaid and Garl's name unspoken the same number of days.

| T071/T072 | Count carried 317 → 318 → 319 → 320 exact, six months and one hundred and thirty-seven through one hundred and forty days told by nobody in Low Kiln, Sill and Grath, spoken by no one; three hundred and twenty stood exact at the close and Bone 30 (Day 329), the month's third and last Account-day, stood nine mornings ahead and was not brought early. No market, Cross or bell on Bone 19 or 21. |
| T088 | The carried fire gave four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should stand under the floor at both ends of all three days, its payer unnamed three hundred and eighteen, nineteen and twenty days; the river's water over water at the finger's-width door and the boards' four nails, four and a thumb-width knot were the other two counts in three places that do not become one, and agreeing any two would want a payer put under both and none stood. |
| T058/T079/T100 | Fire before basket at both ends of every day; instruction to the wool and the river wind and never to the basket; *The house will keep it*; the coals told the thaw and turned with the back of a broken pot; the twice-mended pot lifted with the thumb first where the wire crosses the crack with the crack showing and both proverbs to pot and fire; the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed; the fold righted without a look at his face and the thread left; the charcoal unread beneath her finger on top of the shelf and the two gaps unfigured; one glance at the clay jar cold under lead glaze with the hand half over nothing; the dressed grain turned under wool with a progressively lighter touch and no figure; the widow's mark untouched at every hour because none was an opening; five openings in five months are five and not a rule. On Bone 20 the basket stood in the moot-post's finger's width of shade where no slate lay and she stood half a pace off through the reading and the bell. |
| T009/T013/T092 | Garl kept in objects with his name unspoken three hundred and eighteen, nineteen and twenty days: the salt-stiff coat with the left-shoulder crease, the hollow wheel-seat nobody fills, the clean dark line and finer grey called the thaw unswept, the twice-mended pot with its crack showing, the proverbs to the pot and the fire, and the tile debt circling without a name and worse for being uncalled; no collector came up the clay road or went down it on any of these three days. |
| T083/T085 | Three coverings at the yard well in three places called weather and entered nowhere — the stayed frost gone off the north lip while the yard looked elsewhere, the skin on the trough and the silt-clouded plate of ice on its flat stone out of the path of feet — with a finger between every pair and no fourth likeness made a cause (held). |
| T077 | The month's hunts and repairs stayed directions judged by the carrying arm and the weather, never figures: a man come down from Cold Acre with a hare asked what the carrying cost and was told to ask the weather, going off toward the clay road with nobody weighing the hare; a man with a cracked jar in a rope sling was sent to the pot, and the pot, being a pot, said nothing; no entry left and no man standing up in the yard to be asked. The dressed grain lay under wool at the rack end, turned with a still lighter touch and read over by the arithmetic that went up the road without knowing what it cost. |
| T080 | Ilva's ninth hand came once at the well on Bone 20 with clay pale in her nail crescents and grey rack dust in one thumb seam, her hand going toward her sleeve and staying there with the notched strip unread, the open slate a pace away unjoined and no figure coming off the wood; she answered the question put and not the one behind it with *Ask the pot what it cost. I keep the count, not the account*, her eyes going to the asker and her mouth opening after both with a half-beat; offstage on Bone 19 and 21. Hessa's eighth carried the slate up the road edge-on and unread, answering the women with *I don't read it. I carry it*; the three shapings of the Frost 14 well-saying stayed beside her hand with a finger between. Both hands stay their numbers with no tenth; advanced, **not paid**. |
| T101 | Held: the ownerless row question stood at five askings with one shaping and no witness, and no sixth asking came; the Frost 14 well-saying stood at three shapings, not a witness, a confession, a joining or a rule, and did not make Hessa a reader. |
| T035/T031/T065/T095 | The burned slate stood at five tellings with a finger between the fifth and the four, no witness standing, no hand named at any flame, no sixth due on a day that had not earned one and no payer; the claim went on gathering interest against Jorra's ungiven promise while he neither paid nor refused. The shut-room tellings stayed at two and the pot sayings at three with the Smoke 14 note apart. |

The next I don't count*; the ear-sentence stopped at the calling word as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, the Seed 16 breath unspent, the loan uncalled and no collector on the road; the warm loft stone cold in its unmarked pot and unreconciled by not trying, which is not forgiveness. |

*Chapter 89 opens **no new thread**, pays none and closes none. Its one movement is **T015/T041/T047 advanced and not paid** — Bone's second reading makes five arithmetics stand behind one printed figure, five readings five and not one account, the figure read still not the figure paid and no signature on the space, with the finding kept on a place of its own and the finger going between it and the house's not-doings, the covered grain, the four held changes, the two small objects of the hand and the boy's gaps. Statuses stand at the close of Chapter 89: one hundred and one threads (66 planted, 34 open, 1 paid), nothing joined, named, opened, called, spent or ended, and the count crosses into Bone's last tend with **two hundred and sixteen** answers on the sixth place, the count exact at **three hundred and twenty**, five arithmetics behind in Berr's box with one in twelve printed and unchallenged and the figure read still not the figure paid, five openings in five months, five burned-slate tellings with a finger between, nine hands with Ilva's strip unread and no tenth, three shapings with no witness, the row at five askings, the ninth stopping ungiven, the loan uncalled, the twice-mended pot with its crack showing, the dressed grain covered and unfigured, the stayed frost gone and the trough and clouded plate called weather, the stayed-at-the-inch object and the early letting-go two objects on two places and neither made again, six hearings with the seventh place empty, the heard bell beside the told, and four held changes on four places refused standing up as a rule. Forward, not closed.**

Chapter 90 is written and closed: Days 321–323, Bone 22–24, Secondday to Fourthday, Y.H. 813, three lived days in six full scenes, each day opened by its own dated `\daymark` and lived in two scenes well over eight hundred words, nothing skipped, poured into another or summarised. **No new thread was opened, none was paid and none was closed; one hundred and one threads still stand (66 planted, 34 open, 1 paid), unchanged from the close of Chapter 89.** There was no named character with a real role who was not already on a sheet: Corin/Dan, Sella Vail, Tarn, Jorra Vail and Garl-in-objects went on in their old grammar, Ilva was seen once at the yard well on Bone 23, and the Cold Acre hare-carrier, the man with a cracked jar in a rope sling and the woman with a pot at the well were walk-ons with no sheet. There was no market, Cross or bell on any of the three days, nothing from Bone 20's reading came in as sign, lesson, mending, cause or payment, and Bone 30 (Day 329), the month's third and last reading, stood six mornings ahead and was not brought early. **The chapter's one meaningful change, advanced and not paid (T077, T060/T086, T061/T082):** at the rack end on Bone 22 Sella lifted the wool from the dressed grain, took a small handful and let it fall back through her fingers onto the heap instead of spreading it, saying nothing and giving no figure; she did not do it again on Bone 23 or 24, when her fingers went in and came out without closing. The boy read it as a surgeon lifts a dressing's edge and lets it fall, and filed it on a place of its own with a finger between it and the four held changes on four places and a finger between it and his own gaps: not a fifth held change, sign, lesson, mending, cause, sixth arithmetic or rule, with no payer standing, kept because it was true and not because it bought anything. The empty fingers of the two following mornings went beside it as a keeping and not as a second, for two would be a habit and a habit would want a payer. The handful stands as a seed for the far-off hand that will one day lay the district's private keepings together; it is not read, joined, named or spent and nothing is brought forward into a quest. The six answers, the two hundred and seventeenth through the two hundred and twenty-second, were exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air, none a reach, hearing, seventh, stopping, payment, held change, key, power, gift, doctrine or rule, and each a small intake let go whole on the note's finishing, neither early again nor stayed.

There was no market, Cross or bell on any of the three days, nothing from Bone 20's reading came in as sign, lesson, mending, cause or payment, and Bone 30 (Day 329), the month's third and last reading, stood three mornings ahead and was not brought early. **The chapter's one meaningful change, advanced and not paid (T036/T076/T006, T061/T082, T060/T086):** on Bone 26 at the kindling Tarn set the small knife at the edge of its sill where it could be checked and where a man's hand could also slip it off, carried his thumb up the worn mark to the seventh notch at the lip beyond it — the one the house cannot check — and rested it there for the length of one breath. He did not cut it, count it, bring the ear-sentence to the word that would call the loan or spend the Seed 16 breath; he drew the thumb back down to the six where the house could check and said *Six counted. The next I don't count*. He did not make the resting again on Bone 27, when he said *Yes, house* to a man who wanted the thaw early and a man who wanted it late and kept the late because it puts off the paying. The boy read a hand laid on a place a man had decided not to open and left there unopened, and filed it on a place of its own with a finger between it and the nine stoppings, the four held changes, the handful let fall at the rack end on Bone 22 and his own gaps: **not** a tenth stopping, not the seventh year given, not a payment, not a fifth held change, not a hearing, not a near-full answer, not a mending and not a rule, with no payer standing. No new stopping was added — the nine stand at nine with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end, and the loan stays uncalled with no collector up or down the clay road. Foreshadowing planted: the knife at the sill's lip, checked and unchecked, is established in Scene 1 so that the thumb's resting in Scene 4 arrives on ground already laid, and the resting stands as a seed for the far-off hand that will lay the district's private keepings together, unread, unjoined, unnamed and unspent; that far-off hand is not brought nearer. **Nothing paid.**

Chapter 92 is written and closed: Days 327–329, Bone 28–30, Eighthday to Tenthday, Y.H. 813, three lived days in six full scenes, each day opened by its own dated `\daymark` and lived in two scenes well over eight hundred words, nothing skipped, poured into another or summarised. **No new thread was opened, none was paid and none was closed; one hundred and one threads still stand (66 planted, 34 open, 1 paid), unchanged from the close of Chapter 91.** There was no named character with a real role who was not already on a sheet: Corin/Dan, Sella Vail, Tarn, Jorra Vail and Garl-in-objects went on in their old grammar; Ilva was seen once at the yard well on Bone 29, Berr Clay and Hessa Rale were on stage at the Cross and the road on Bone 30, and the Cold Acre hare-carrier, the cracked-jar man, the woman who asked Ilva at the well, the woman with a basket of kindling and the two fence-menders were walk-ons with no sheet. There was no market, Cross or bell on Bone 28 or 29, nothing from Bone 20's reading came in as sign, lesson, mending, cause or payment, and Bone went out without a boundary drawn while neither of the district's two habits of naming its months was corrected. **The chapter's one meaningful change, advanced and not paid (T015/T041/T047):** on Bone 30 the month's third and last reading came to the Cross. Berr Clay came up short off the clay road with the red wool cord of his office folded square under his coat and the sweet green of tasted lead glaze at one mouth-corner, under the hot clay the smell of nothing at all; he wiped his thumb twice on his apron before touching nothing, held a narrow slate unopened with the writing inward, passed a finger over the figure, read *One in twelve, as the notice says* low into the goers-by and sent the figure twice over the basket — once for the moot and once for the late households — called the levy, denied it with *The levy is called. It is not called by me* and *your house*, never *I*, said something low to the block about kindness being entered, and went off up the clay road with the box locked and Bone's third true subtraction inside beside the other five, believing he had done a kindness. **Six arithmetics of the year now stand behind one printed figure; six are six and not one account**, the figure read still not the figure paid, no signature on the space and a rule made from six refused for want of a payer. The boy kept the finding on a place of its own with no payer, not a lesson, grievance, mending, doctrine or rule, and did not lay it across the house's not-doings, the covered grain, the four held changes, the handful, the thumb's resting, the two small objects of the hand or his own gaps — the edges nearly touched and the finger went between. The reading answered nothing for the hand that went in on Seed 15, the man carried out on Day 188, the dressed grain under wool or the carried fire's missing fifth. The boy took the opening by the small sounds and filed it on a sixth place of its own with a finger's width around it, noting only that the fifth pull was still missing and joining it to none of the six arithmetics, the bell's gap, the covered grain, the handful, the thumb's resting or the two small objects of his own hand. Answers 235 through 240 were entered one per scene and **two hundred and forty honest answers** stand on the sixth place at the close, each an object and not a power; **three hundred and thirty-two** stands exact, complete, unspent and spoken by nobody, six months and one hundred and fifty-two days told by nobody, the carried fire's fifth unpaid the same number with its payer unnamed and Garl's name unspoken the same; Ash 10 (Day 339), the dark month's first Account-day and market, stands seven mornings beyond the close and was not brought early. Forward, not closed.

Chapter 94 is written and closed: Days 333–335, Ash 4–6, Fourthday to Sixthday, Y.H. 813, three lived days in six full scenes, each day opened by its own dated `\daymark` and lived in two scenes well over eight hundred words, nothing skipped, poured into another or summarised. **No new thread was opened, none was paid and none was closed; one hundred and one threads still stand (66 planted, 34 open, 1 paid), unchanged from the close of Chapter 93.** There was no named character with a real role who was not already on a sheet: Corin/Dan, Sella Vail, Tarn, Jorra Vail, Ilva, Hessa Rale and Garl-in-objects went on in their old grammar, and the Cold Acre hare-carrier, the cracked-jar man, the woman with a cost-question, the woman who asked Ilva at the well, the woman with a basket of kindling, the two fence-menders, the woman who asked the runner what she carried and the two ownerless voices were walk-ons with no sheet. There was no market, Cross or bell on Ash 4, 5 or 6, no collector came up or down the clay road — Hessa coming down it on Ash 6 is a slate-runner returning and is never mistaken for a collector — nothing from Ash 1, 2 or 3 crossed as sign, lesson, mending, cause or payment, and Ash kept its middle days without a boundary drawn while neither of the district's two habits of naming its months was corrected. **The chapter's three movements, all advanced and NOT paid:** (1) on Ash 5 an ownerless voice over the boards of the Clay Yard, on the same breath as the price of barley and the weather, said for the first time that the slate that burned was burned in the room with the damper shut — the Greybank saying of the counting room shut in the war spoken without a date and without a witness standing anywhere to be asked; the boy filed it as a first joining of the burned slate to the shut room on a place of its own, **not a sixth telling of the slate** (five stay five), **not a third telling of the room** (two stay two), not a hearing, seventh, stopping, payment, cause, confession or rule, with no payer and no name under it; the claim goes on gathering interest against Jorra's ungiven promise, which is neither given nor withdrawn, and the betrayal that waits to be called is not called here (T035/T031/T065/T095 advanced, not paid). (2) On Ash 5 an ownerless voice at the well gave the Frost 14 well-saying a **fourth shaping**: the runner who carried the figure had come back down the road with the slate turned toward her, with no owner standing, no name, no figure, no confession and no cause; four shapings are still not a witness, no fifth came, Ilva drawing a pace away was expressly not made the speaker, her strip was not joined to the saying and Hessa was not made a reader (T080 advanced, not paid). (3) On Ash 6 Hessa came down the clay road with the writing turned toward herself for the first time, still edge-on, still unread, no figure off it and no choosing made; the boy filed the turning on a place of its own beside the fourth shaping with a finger between and refused to join saying to sighting, make a fifth shaping, make her a reader, make the sighting a payment or pay the claim; her eighth hand stays eighth with no tenth (T080 advanced, not paid). The two Ash 5 movements and the Ash 6 sighting are held on separate places with a finger between them and between them and Ilva's strip, Berr's thumb, the soft-cuffed clerk's inward slate and the charcoal under the shelf. Answers 241 through 246 were entered one per scene and **two hundred and forty-six honest answers** stand on the sixth place, the count exact at **three hundred and thirty-five** — six months and one hundred and fifty-five days told by nobody — the carried fire's fifth unpaid three hundred and thirty-five days with its payer unnamed and Garl's name unspoken the same number. The burned slate stays at five with no sixth and no witness, the shut-room tellings at two and no third, the row at five askings with no sixth, the well-saying at four shapings and no fifth, nine record-first hands with no tenth, nine stoppings with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, six openings in six months with no seventh made due, the widow's mark last touched at the kiln mouth on Ash 2 and not touched on Ash 4, 5 or 6, six hearings beside and never among with the seventh place empty, and the heard bell in its square beside the told. Nothing was joined, named, opened, called, paid or ended. Forward, not closed.**

Chapter 95 is written and closed: Days 336–338, Ash 7–9, Seventhday to Ninthday, Y.H. 813, a normal three-day chapter in the dark month's last tending days, each day opened by its own `\daymark` and lived in two full scenes, nothing skipped, poured into another or summarised. **It opened no new thread, paid none and closed none; one hundred and one threads stand at the close as stood at the close of Chapter 94 (66 planted, 34 open, 1 paid).** There was no new named character with a real role: Dan/Corin, Sella, Tarn, Jorra, Ilva and Garl-in-objects were the only figures with sheets, the Cold Acre hare-carrier, the cracked-jar man, two cost-questioners, the kindling-questioner, two fence-menders and Ilva's asker were walk-ons entered in `characters/_minor.md`, Hessa was offstage for the whole chapter, no runner was seen on any road after Ash 6, no collector came up or down the clay road, and no market, Cross or bell came on any of the three days. Ash kept its last tending days without a boundary drawn, neither habit of naming the months was corrected, and Ash 10 (Day 339), the dark month's first Account-day and market, stood one morning beyond the close and was named only as a date. **The chapter's one meaningful change, advanced and NOT paid (T009/T013/T092, T060/T086):** at the going of the light on Ash 9, when Sella lifted the twice-mended pot from the pot board, her thumb went to the wire where it crossed the crack and stayed one breath longer than the lift required before she let the weight come on the handle, the hairline of the original break left showing between the old-brass staple and the tighter wire. She said both proverbs to the pot and the fire and never to a person, improved in the keeping and very likely not as good as the man said them; repair stayed apart from restoration, for a restored thing hides the hand that handled it and a mended thing leaves that hand showing. The boy took the held interval apart by what was there and by what was not — a distance between the thumb's arrival and its moving on that buys nothing at two inches of air and is not a gift, for a gift wants a giver and nobody had given — and filed it on a place of its own **beside** the staying at the inch, the early letting-go, the handful let fall at the rack end, Tarn's thumb's resting on the uncut seventh and the sixth opening at the kiln mouth, with a finger between every pair. It is **expressly NOT a sixth held object**, not a habit, a way, a hearing, a near-full answer, a sign, a mending, a cause, a payer or a rule, not to be made again, not joined to the charcoal, Ilva's strip, the Ash 5 joining, the fourth shaping, the Ash 6 turned writing, the covered grain or his own gaps, and not to be spent or promoted by the reading that follows. It gathers toward the far-off hand that will lay the district's private keepings together, and that hand is still far off and is not his. No payer stands under it. The count itself is the chapter's other honest movement: answers **247, 248, 249, 250, 251 and 252** were entered one per scene, the two hundred and fifty-second in the small hours of Ash 9, and **two hundred and fifty-two honest answers** stand on the sixth place, each an object and not a power.

Chapter 96 is written and closed: Days 339–341, Ash 10–12, Tenthday to Secondday, Y.H. 813, three lived days in six full scenes, with Ash 10 (Day 339), the dark month's first Account-day and market, earned by its own morning and no market, Cross or bell on Ash 11 or 12. **It opened no new thread, paid none and closed none; one hundred and one threads stand at the close (66 planted, 34 open, 1 paid), unchanged from the close of Chapter 95.** No new named character with a real role appeared: Dan/Corin, Sella Vail, Tarn, Jorra Vail, Berr Clay, Hessa Rale, Ilva and Garl-in-objects went on in their old grammar, and the two hundred at the reading block, the woman who asked the runner, the man with a number in his fist, the soft-cuffed clerk at the landing, the green-mouthed woman at the pot board, the foundling at the market's edge, the Cold Acre hare-carrier, the cracked-jar man, the woman with a cost-question, Ilva's asker, the kindling-questioner and the two fence-menders were walk-ons entered in `characters/_minor.md`. Nothing from Ash 10's reading crossed under any roof as sign, lesson, mending, cause or payment; no collector came up or went down the clay road on any of the three days; Hessa taking the slate up the road is a runner's errand and never a collector; Ash kept its days without a boundary drawn while neither of the district's two habits of naming its months was corrected; and Ash 20 (Day 349), the month's second Account-day, stood eight mornings ahead and was named only as a date. **The chapter's one meaningful change, advanced and NOT paid (T015/T041/T047):** Berr Clay came up short off the clay road with the red wool cord of his office folded square under his coat and the sweetish green of tasted lead glaze at one mouth-corner, wiped his thumb twice before touching nothing, passed a finger over the figure, read *One in twelve, as the notice says*, called the levy, denied it with *The levy is called. It is not called by me* and *your house*, never *I*, said something low to the block about kindness being entered, and went off up the clay road with the box locked and Ash's first true subtraction inside, believing he had done a kindness. **Seven arithmetics of the year — the three of Frost, the first, second and third of Bone and Ash's first — now stand behind one printed figure; seven are seven and not one account**, the figure read still not the figure paid, no signature on the space, the finding kept on a place of its own with no payer and not laid across the house's not-doings, the dressed grain covered under wool, the five held objects, the pot-crack resting, the handful, the thumb's resting, the two small objects of the hand or the boy's gaps; the edges came near to touching and the finger went between, and no doctrine stood up, for a doctrine is an account that has found a payer and none stood. The reading answered nothing for the hand that went in on Seed 15, the man carried out on Day 188, the grain read over by a number that did not know its cost or the carried fire's missing fifth.

Chapter 97 is written and closed: Days 342–344, Ash 13–15, Thirdday to Fifthday, Y.H. 813, three lived days in six full scenes, all ordinary tending days with no market, Cross or bell and no collector up or down the clay road. **It opened no new thread, paid none and closed none; one hundred and one threads stand at the close (66 planted, 34 open, 1 paid), unchanged from the close of Chapter 96.** No new named character with a real role appeared: Dan/Corin, Sella Vail, Tarn, Jorra Vail, Ilva and Garl-in-objects went on in their old grammar, and the Cold Acre hare-carrier, the cracked-jar man, the woman with a basket of kindling, the two fence-menders and the woman waiting her turn at Ilva's well were walk-ons entered in `characters/_minor.md`; Berr Clay, Hessa Rale and all farther-off characters were offstage and Dessa Silt stays dead. Nothing from Ash 10–12 crossed under any roof as sign, lesson, mending, cause or payment, no runner was seen on any road, and Ash 20 (Day 349), the month's second Account-day, stood five mornings ahead and was named only as a date. **The chapter's one meaningful change, advanced and NOT paid (T036/T076/T006, held with T061/T082):** on the afternoon of Ash 14 at the kindling Tarn set the small knife where it could be checked, passed his hand over it as the house checks, and let the hand stay at the sill a breath longer than the check required before taking it away — a breath with a shape to it, held at the top of the reach where the unspent Seed 16 breath had stayed since the dark. He cut nothing, counted nothing, brought the ear-sentence no closer to the calling word, spent no breath and did not make the thumb's resting of Bone 26 again; the loan stayed uncalled. The boy filed the held breath on a place of its own beside the staying at the inch, the early letting-go, the handful, the thumb's resting, the sixth opening and the pot-crack resting, with a finger between every pair — expressly not a sixth held object, not a seventh of anything, not a tenth stopping, not the seventh year given, not a habit, way, hearing, near-full answer, sign, mending, cause, payment or rule, with no payer standing. It was checked where it had been put on Ash 15 and was not made again or joined to the charcoal, Ilva's strip, the Ash 5 joining, the fourth shaping, the turned writing, the grain or any of his own gaps. It gathers toward the far-off hand that will one day lay the district's private keepings together — a hand that is not his and is still far off. Nothing was paid.
