Chapter 98 is written and closed: Days 345–347, Ash 16–18, Sixthday to Eighthday, Y.H. 813, three lived days in six full scenes, each day opened by its own `\daymark` and lived in two scenes well over eight hundred words, nothing skipped, poured into another or summarised; all three were ordinary tending days with no market, Cross or bell and no collector up or down the clay road. **It opened no new thread, paid none and closed none; one hundred and one threads stand at the close (66 planted, 34 open, 1 paid), unchanged from the close of Chapter 97.** No new named character with a real role appeared: Dan/Corin, Sella Vail, Tarn, Jorra Vail, Ilva and Garl-in-objects went on in their old grammar, and the Cold Acre hare-carrier, the cracked-jar man, the woman with a basket of kindling, the two fence-menders and the woman waiting her turn at Ilva's well were walk-ons entered in `characters/_minor.md`; the ownerless voice over the boards was given no sheet and no owner standing to be asked; Berr Clay, Hessa Rale and all farther-off characters were offstage and Dessa Silt stays dead. Nothing from Ash 16, 17 or 18 crossed under any roof as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer; no runner was seen on any road, and Ash 20 (Day 349), the month's second Account-day, stood two mornings ahead and was named only as a date. **The chapter's one meaningful change, advanced and NOT paid (T035/T031/T065/T095 with T101):** on the afternoon of Ash 17 an ownerless voice came over the boards from the direction of Slate Row, spoken over the boards and not into the basket, and gave a word about a room shut with the damper closed and a slate burned over a man nobody named — no room named, no hand at any flame, no figure, no date standing and nobody standing in any doorway to be asked. The weather answered first and the price of barley after it, and the voice went up the terrace while the boards lay where they lay. The boy opened the saying as a surgeon opens a wound and found no witness at the bottom of it; he filed it on a place of its own **beside** the Ash 5 joining of the burned slate to the shut room with a finger between every pair, a further shaping of that joining and an advancement of the finding that a place wants a witness and a witness is a day somebody stands somewhere and can be asked — expressly **not** a sixth telling of the burned slate (five), not a third telling of the shut room (two), not a sixth asking of the row (five), not a fifth shaping of the well-saying (four), not a hearing, not a seventh of the full note, not a cause, not a confession, not a joining, not a witness, not a reader, not a name and not a payment, with no payer standing under it. Jorra grew quieter when the direction went around and the household straightened around the quiet without an order; his promise stayed neither given nor withdrawn. Ilva was at the well that afternoon with her ninth hand nine and the strip unread and is expressly not the speaker. The hand answered six times, answers 265 through 270, each a restraint and not a payment, and **two hundred and seventy** honest answers stand on the sixth place, each an object and not a power; the count closes at **three hundred and forty-seven exact**, six months and one hundred and sixty-seven days told by nobody, the carried fire's fifth unpaid and Garl's name unspoken the same number. No eighth arithmetic, sixth hearing, sixth held object, sixth telling, third shut-room telling, sixth asking, fifth shaping, tenth hand or tenth stopping came; nothing was opened, joined by a standing hand, named, called, paid or ended. Forward, not closed.

Chapter 101 is written and closed: Days 354–356, Ash 25–27, Fifthday to Seventhday, Y.H. 813, three lived days in six full scenes, two to a day, each day opened by its own `\daymark` in the first scene of that day and each scene well over eight hundred words, nothing skipped, poured into another or summarised; all three were ordinary tending days with no market, Cross or bell, no collector on the clay road and no runner on any road, and nothing from Ash 22, 23 or 24 crossed as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer. The chapter's one meaningful change is **T062/T035/T031 and T061/T082 advanced and NOT paid**: on Ash 26, at the damper, after the tongue had been moved, the sentence finished and the household straightened around the waiting — after the work was done, not before — Jorra's bent finger stayed in the cold iron a breath longer than the work required. The boy filed the extra interval on a place of its own with a finger between it and the five held objects, the pot-crack resting, the hand-at-the-sill breath and his own gaps: a private keeping gathered once and not spent, expressly not a sixth held object, not a seventh, not an eighth of anything, not a habit, not a way, not a hearing, not a near-full answer, not a mending, not a cause, not a payment and not a rule, with no payer standing under it, gathering toward the far-off hand that will lay the district's private keepings together, and that hand not his. On Ash 27 the finger came out and the interval was found where it had been put and **not made again**, for a second would be a habit and a third a way, both of which want a payer and none stood. **T080 advanced and not paid**: Ilva's ninth record-first hand at the well on Ash 26, strip unread, no tenth filed, answering the question put and not the one behind it and expressly not the speaker of any voice. The hand answered six times, **283 through 288**, and the count closed at **356 exact**, six months and one hundred and seventy-six days told by nobody, the carried fire's fifth unpaid and Garl's name unspoken the same number.

Chapter 102 is written and closed: Days 357–359, Ash 28–30, Eighthday to Tenthday, Y.H. 813, three lived days in six full scenes, two to a day, each day opened by its own `\daymark` in the first scene of that day and each scene well over eight hundred words, nothing skipped, poured into another or summarised. Ash 28 and 29 were ordinary tending days with no market, Cross or bell, no collector on the clay road and no runner on any road; Ash 30 (Day 359) was the dark month's third and last Account-day and market, earned by its own morning. **It opened no new thread, paid none and closed none; one hundred and one threads stand at the close (66 planted, 34 open, 1 paid), unchanged from the close of Chapter 101.** No new named character with a real role appeared: Dan/Corin, Sella Vail, Tarn, Jorra Vail, Ilva, Berr Clay, Hessa Rale and Garl-in-objects went on in their old grammar, and the Cold Acre hare-carrier, the cracked-jar man, the woman with kindling, the two fence-menders, the woman who asked Ilva at the well, the two hundred at the Cross, the soft-cuffed clerk at the out-of-line landing, the silent green-mouthed woman at the pot board and the foundling's shape at the market's edge were walk-ons entered in `characters/_minor.md`; no ownerless voice came over the boards on any of the three days, no collector came up or down the clay road and Dessa Silt stays dead. Nothing from Ash 25, 26 or 27 crossed as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer. **The chapter's one meaningful change, advanced and NOT paid (T015/T041/T047):** on Ash 30 the district's third reading of the dark month came to the Cross; Berr Clay read *one in twelve, as the notice says* twice over the basket, called the levy and denied it with *The levy is called. It is not called by me* and *your house*, never I, taking himself out of his own sentence as a surgeon draws a hand from a field before the dressing goes on; he said something low to the block about kindness being entered, to which the block answered nothing, and went off with the box locked and Ash's third true subtraction inside, believing he had done a kindness with no anger and no triumph in him. **Nine arithmetics of the year — the three of Frost, the first, second and third of Bone, and Ash's first, second and third — now stand behind one unsigned figure; nine are nine and not one account**, one in twelve printed and unchallenged, the figure read still not the figure paid and no signature on the space. The boy set the finding on a place of its own with no payer standing, expressly **not** laid across the house's not-doings, the covered grain, the five held objects, the pot-crack resting, the hand-at-the-sill breath, the holding of Ash 26, the Ash 5 joining, the Ash 17 direction, the Ash 23 direction or his own kept gaps; the edges came near to touching and the finger went between, and no doctrine stood up out of nine, for a doctrine is an account that has found a payer and none stood. The reading answered none of the held questions. Six answers were filed, 289 through 294, and **two hundred and ninety-four honest answers** stand on the sixth place, each an object and not a power. Count closes at **three hundred and fifty-nine exact**, six months and one hundred and seventy-nine days told by nobody, the carried fire's fifth unpaid and Garl's name unspoken the same number. Paid off: the ninth arithmetic, a date since the first of Ash, earned its own morning and went up in the locked box; nothing was opened, joined by a standing hand, named, called, paid or ended under any roof.

Chapter 103 is written and closed: Days 360–362, Stone 1–3, Firstday to Thirdday, Y.H. 813, three lived days in six full scenes, two to a day, each day opened by its own `\daymark` in the first scene of that day and each scene well over eight hundred words, nothing skipped, poured into another or summarised. All three were ordinary tending days with no market, Cross or bell, no collector on the clay road and no runner on any road, and the deep-winter month in which he was born came on without a boundary drawn while neither of the district's two habits of naming its months was corrected. **It opened no new thread, paid none and closed none; one hundred and one threads stand at the close (66 planted, 34 open, 1 paid), unchanged from the close of Chapter 102.** No new named character with a real role appeared: Dan/Corin, Sella Vail, Tarn, Jorra Vail, Ilva and Garl-in-objects went on in their old grammar, and the Cold Acre hare-carrier, the cracked-jar man, the woman with kindling, the two fence-menders, the woman who asked Ilva at the well, Berr's box up the clay road and Hessa's road were carried as directions or walk-ons entered in `characters/_minor.md`; no ownerless voice came over the boards on any of the three days, no collector came up or went down the clay road, and Dessa Silt stays dead. Nothing from Ash 28, 29 or 30 crossed as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer. **The chapter's one meaningful change, advanced and NOT paid (T083/T085 with T078):** on the afternoon of Stone 1 the river's note under the finger's-width door came no longer water over water in the open but low under a skin — the Ilm had taken its winter ice from bank to bank — and a man come down from Cold Acre with a hare across his shoulders, asked what the ice would cost, told the asker to ask the weather, which had laid it on and would take it off; no slate was opened and no figure came. The boy filed the new note on a place of its own beside water over water: a covering put on by the cold and taken off by the cold, entered nowhere, expressly not a sixth low thing standing up as a rule, not a hearing (a hearing wants a source standing and none stood), not a seventh of the full note, not a fourth of the three coverings and not a sign, lesson, cause, payment or payer, with no payer standing. It was found where put on Stone 2 and 3 and not made again, gathering toward the deep winter, Stone 5's first firing, the birthday on Stone 7 and the Hearth Drawing on Stone 12 and paying none of them. **T080 advanced and not paid:** Ilva's ninth record-first hand came once at the well on Stone 2, strip unread, no tenth made and expressly not the speaker of any voice. The hand answered six times, 295 through 300, and **three hundred honest answers** stand on the sixth place, each an object and not a power and not one standing up and calling itself a doctrine; the count closes at **362 exact**, six months and one hundred and eighty-two days told by nobody, with the carried fire's fifth unpaid and Garl's name unspoken 360, 361 and 362 days, six openings in six months and not a rule with no seventh made due, nine arithmetics behind one unsigned figure with all three Ash subtractions locked and unread, the burned slate at five, the shut-room tellings at two, the row at five askings, nine record-first hands and nine stoppings with no tenth, the loan uncalled, and the holding of Ash 26 gathered once and not made again. Forward, not closed.

Chapter 105 is written and closed: Days 366–368, Stone 7–9, Seventhday to Ninthday, Y.H. 813, three lived days in six full scenes, two to a day, each day opened by its own `\daymark` in the first scene of that day and each scene well over eight hundred words, nothing skipped, poured into another or summarised. All three were ordinary tending days with no market, Cross or bell, no collector on the clay road and no runner on any road, and the deep-winter month came round to the day a year before without a boundary drawn while neither of the district's two habits of naming its months was corrected — the older women naming it by the weather, the slatemen by the count of Account-days. **It opened no new thread, paid none and closed none; one hundred and one threads stand at the close (66 planted, 34 open, 1 paid), unchanged from the close of Chapter 104.** No new named character with a real role appeared: Dan/Corin, Sella Vail, Tarn, Jorra Vail and Garl-in-objects went on in their old grammar, and the Cold Acre hare-carrier, the cracked-jar man, the woman with kindling and the two fence-menders were walk-ons entered in `characters/_minor.md`; Ilva, Hessa Rale, Berr Clay, Mira Silt, Orra Weir, Alda Reed, Rusk, Marra, the soft-handed man from Slate Row, the green-mouthed woman and the foundling were offstage, Dessa Silt stays dead, and no ownerless voice came over the boards on any of the three days. Nothing from Stone 4, 5 or 6 crossed as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer. **The chapter's one meaningful change, advanced and NOT paid (T071/T072 with T088):** Stone 7 (Day 366) was the boy's first birthday in this life, a whole year stood edge to edge in the only count that is exact, and it was lived as an ordinary day — no party, cake, figure, recognition, threshold or line crossed, nobody under any roof who would know what a number counts, no loaf set aside and no word over the basket. He kept three hundred and sixty-six, three hundred and sixty-seven and three hundred and sixty-eight exactly and did not stand the completed year up as a line, and Days 367 and 368 proved the birthday left no residue: the house woke to the same hearth grammar on both mornings, and nobody's failure to name it was either a cruelty or a mercy that could be entered on a slate.

Chapter 113 is written and closed: Days 390–392, Kindling, Weighing and the Long Night, Y.H. 813, the first three of the Five, three lived days in six full scenes, two to a day, each opened by its own `\daymark` and each lived on the page, nothing skipped, poured into another or summarised. **It opened no new thread, paid none and closed none; one hundred and one threads stand at the close (66 planted, 34 open, 1 paid), unchanged from the close of Chapter 112.** No new named character with a real role appeared: Dan/Corin, Sella Vail, Tarn and Jorra Vail walk the page, Garl Vail is kept in objects, and the Kindling collector, the clean-voice officer and the neighbours are walk-ons with no sheet. The Five belong to no month and have names, not tend-days; no market was held in them and the year was not said to turn on any of them. **The chapter's one meaningful change is T080/T090 advanced and NOT paid:** a collector took the year's first measure with an ordinary writing hand and no pause in it, and the boy filed that hand on a tray of its own — not Marra, not the Court-table clerk, not the Fishstairs clerk, not the Drawing collector and expressly not a tenth — while planting, unspoken, the reason that will one day be remembered against the taker, that he keeps the world alive by taking what is already going; a clean voice announced a whole return for somebody absent and left a name and a silence the household would not fill, and on the Long Night a neighbour's story left a name standing empty, both filed among the gaps with no reader, witness, payer or doctrine standing up. The first present-tense break in eighty-eight chapters came once on that clean voice's form — a page over the speakers, a white room that does not look up, hands that stay in the field — untagged, unanticipated, paying nothing, and the grammar fell straight back into the past.

## Chapter 123 — The Figure That Went Back to the Sleeve (Days 420–422)

Chapter 123 is written and closed: Days 420–422, Ilmen 26–28, Y.H. 814, Sixthday to Eighthday, three ordinary tending days lived one at a time in six full scenes, two to a day, each opened by its own dated `\daymark`; no market, Cross, bell, Account-day, collector or runner came on any of them, and Ilmen 30 (Day 424), the month's third and last reading, stands two mornings beyond the close and is not brought. The hand is flat on the fold on answer 420 at the close, the count exact at 422, six months and two hundred and forty-two days told by nobody. It opened **no new thread**, paid none and closed none; one hundred and two threads stand as they stood at the close of Chapter 122 (67 planted, 34 open, 1 paid). Nothing from Ilmen 26, 27 or 28 crossed under the Vail roof, out of the yard or up the clay road as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer, and the not-crossing was itself kept.

Ilva drew with the pail against her knee, the rope stiff in the dry cold giving its small rasp, clay dried pale in her nail crescents and finer rack dust worked into the seam of one thumb she did not scrub out; people noticed the pail first and the sleeve not at all. Chapter 124 is written and closed: Days 423–425, Ilmen 29–30, Silt 1, Y.H. 814, Ninthday to Tenthday to Firstday, three days lived one at a time in six full scenes, two to a day, each of the three days opened by its own dated `\daymark`; Ilmen 29 had no market, Cross, bell, Account-day, collector or runner, Ilmen 30 earned its third and last reading and market by its own morning, and Silt 1 came on without a boundary drawn with neither of the district's two habits of naming its months set right or left. The hand is flat on the fold on answer 426 at the close, the count exact at 425, six months and two hundred and forty-five days told by nobody. It opened **no new thread**, paid none and closed none; one hundred and two threads stand as they stood at the close of Chapter 123 (67 planted, 34 open, 1 paid). Nothing from any of the three days crossed under the Vail roof, out of the yard or up the clay road as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer, and the not-crossing was itself kept. **The chapter's one large change, advanced and NOT paid (T015/T041/T047):** on Ilmen 30 Berr Clay came up short off the clay road to the reading block under the moot-post with the red wool cord of his office folded square under his coat and the sweetish green of tasted lead glaze at one mouth-corner, under the hot clay of him the smell of nothing at all; he wiped his thumb twice before touching nothing, held a narrow slate unopened to his forearm with the writing inward, passed a finger over the figure through his sleeve, let his eyes rest on the writing a breath longer than the writing required, read *One in twelve, as the notice says* low into the goers-by and sent the figure twice over the basket, once for the moot and once for the households that came late, never looking into it. He called the levy and denied it — *The levy is called. It is not called by me*; *your house*, never *I* — taking himself out of his own sentence as a surgeon draws a hand from a field before the dressing goes on; to the man with the number in a shut fist he sent the number into a slate at the watch and it went fist to mouth to shoulder and arrived nowhere; something low he said to the block about kindness being entered, in the tone of a man setting a cup where a cup belongs, with no anger, no triumph and no payer standing; and he went off up the clay road toward High Kiln with the cord folded, the narrow slate under his arm and the box locked, Ilmen's third true subtraction inside, believing he had done a kindness. **Three readings of the year now stand behind one unsigned figure** — Ilmen 10, 20 and 30 — three are three and not one account, the first is not made a thirteenth by the second or the third, the figure read is still not the figure paid, no signature stands on the space and no doctrine comes out of three; the twelve old arithmetics are not laid across the three to make a row come out even, for paper is not a payer and the key went up in a coat pocket that never comes back down. His kindness grows toward the day it will be remembered against him and his *your house* toward the day a hand that was in a field must be found to have gone away before the dressing went on. **The second plant, years ahead and unspent — the first reaching of the adult romance (T050/T051 and T033/T034 advanced and NOT paid):** at the pot board across the square on Ilmen 30 a woman with clay dried pale in the crescents of her nails and a pale cord-mark on the back of one hand where something tight and long had once been worn took up a cup, turned it a quarter without lifting it and set it back exactly where it stood; she said nothing and went off with the light, never Fenna in the narration. At the market's edge a foundling in cast-offs with silt dried pale in his wrists, a gap in his grin and a green sliver at his throat catching light and going dull turned his head a half-beat after a pot's knock and note and stopped in the middle of the turn, given no dialogue and never Ulda in the narration. The boy filed the two as sightings on separate trays — a colour and a shape, with the whole square of noise between them — no loaf, slate, sale, word or name passing, no finger laid from one to the other, no eighth of either, no fourth likeness made a cause and no witness, reader or payer standing. Fenna's ear and Ulda's loaf and sale to a clerk in a Waiting Room stay years ahead; the adult romance is planted and never spent in these chapters. On Silt 1 a walk-on girl with clay to her wrists passed a cup from hand to hand at the yard without lifting it from the board and set it back where it stood; she is a walk-on echo, not a third sighting and not a fourth of either tray. Both sightings stayed on their trays and did not cross under the roof as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer.

## Chapter 125 — A Finger's Width Short (Days 426–428)

Chapter 125 is written and closed: Days 426–428, Silt 2–4, Y.H. 814, Secondday to Fourthday, three ordinary tending days lived one at a time in six full scenes, two to a day, each of the three opened by its own dated `\daymark`; no market, Cross, bell, Account-day, called collector or runner came on any of them, and nothing from Ilmen 30's third reading or its two market sightings crossed under the Vail roof as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer. The hand is flat on the fold on answer 432 at the close, the count exact at 428, six months and two hundred and forty-eight days told by nobody. It opened **no new thread**, paid none and closed none; one hundred and two threads stand as they stood at the close of Chapter 124 (67 planted, 34 open, 1 paid). **The chapter's one meaningful change, advanced and NOT paid (T097 with T060/T086, brushing T100 and T015/T041/T047):** at the Vail loaf shelf in the afternoon of Silt 3 a neighbour with a pot hitched against her hip reached past the bare board before her eyes found the basket, the way neighbours had reached before; her finger went along the top of the shelf where the charcoal tally lay beneath, tracing the front edge without going beneath it and without reading what lay there, and then, without her seeing it, went in the direction of the empty place at the boy's ear and stopped a finger's width short of the fold. She named the row's old gap a thing the turning of the month brought in and the empty place a child's appetite in one breath, as one says the weather, made two rooms one absence without seeing she had done it and went off with her pot. He took the reaching apart by the order of its parts — hand to board before eye to basket, mouth after both, the half-beat standing in the gap where a joining would have stood — and filed it on a place of its own beside the earlier shapings and the far-off finger that has not come: a further shaping, advanced and NOT paid, no joining, no name, no figure, no third gap, no fourth likeness made a cause, no finger of his laid across the space, no reading or copying of the charcoal, no account and no payer standing, not made his own and not laid across the twelve arithmetics, the three readings gone up the road, the printed figure, the fifth shaping, the offered figure or the clerk's entered figure. On Silt 4 it was not repeated, made a custom, a sixth shaping, a witness, a reader or a payer.

## Chapter 127 — The Fourth Figure (Days 432–434)

Chapter 127 is written and closed: Days 432–434, Silt 8–10, Y.H. 814, Eighthday to Tenthday, three days lived one at a time in six full scenes, two to a day, each of the three opened by its own dated `\daymark`; Silt 8 and 9 were ordinary tending days with no market, Cross, bell, Account-day, called collector or runner, and Silt 10 was the month's first Account-day and market and the year's fourth reading, earned by its own morning and not made a threshold, a signing or an eighth opening. Nothing from the reported second slate of Silt 6 or the hair-thin thaw of Silt 7 crossed under the Vail roof on any of the three days as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer, neither was repeated or made a custom, and the account-day was not made to answer the neighbour's near-reaching at the shelf. The hand is flat on the fold on answer 444 at the close and the count exact at 434, six months and two hundred and fifty-four days told by nobody. It opened **no new thread**, paid none and closed none; one hundred and two threads stand as they stood at the close of Chapter 126 (67 planted, 34 open, 1 paid). **The chapter's one large change, advanced and NOT paid, is T015/T041/T047:** on Silt 10 Berr Clay reads *one in twelve, as the notice says* twice over the basket, calls the levy, denies it with *your house*, never *I*, sends a fist-number to a slate at the watch where it arrives nowhere, says something low to the block about kindness being entered, and goes off up the road with Silt's fourth true subtraction locked in his box and the key gone up in a coat pocket that never comes back down, believing he has done a kindness with no anger and no triumph. Four readings of the year stand behind one unsigned figure and four are four and not one account. Nothing else is joined, named, opened, called, paid, forgiven or ended.
